 LYNCHBURG Va. (WSET) — For SNAP recipients in Lynchburg, stolen benefits can mean suddenly having less food for their families.
 Susan Cooper said her mother’s benefits disappeared overnight. “I was shocked,” Cooper said.
 “Someone put a skimmer on the machine where she had used it at a Dollar Tree. The next morning, she checked it: all gone. They stole all of her EBT,” she said.
 Deondre Smith said he knows what that loss feels like. “I was once scammed for over $300. So, I wasn't able to feed my kids or my family,” Smith said.
 Smith was among hundreds of people who turned to local food pantries for help when Lynchburg SNAP theft rose drastically in late summer of 2026.
 “I just felt like they just took food out of my kids' mouth," Smith said.
 In August, more than $62,000 in SNAP benefits were reported stolen in Lynchburg. 
 “You could have a family receiving up to $1,500 in SNAP and their benefits. It would post at midnight, and by 2 a.m. they were gone,” said Selina Morgan, a client service supervisor with Lynchburg Human Services.
 SEE ALSO: Lynchburg nursing home named Virginia’s best in Newsweek ranking 
 The reported amount stolen fell to about $33,800 in September and nearly $20,000 in October, according to Lynchburg Human Services. The decline followed the rollout of new SNAP cards in mid-September.
 Morgan said the old cards relied on a card number, while the new cards add an expiration date, a three-digit security code and a personal identification number. Recipients can also tap the new cards instead of swiping them.
 “Our debit cards have these layers of safety, and our credit cards have these layers. And for so long EBT didn't. It was just a card number,” Morgan said.
 Morgan said the department has not received a single report of SNAP fraud involving one of the new chip cards.
 The following list shows the SNAP skimming totals by month in 2026 recorded by Lynchburg Human Services:
 January — $3,141.52
 February — $2,633.98
 March — $711.46
 April — $1,145.83
 May — $1,675.05
 June — $1,531.15
 July — $3,598.09
 August — $62,420.02
 September — $33,838.76
 October — $19,973.14
 Recipients said the added security is already making a difference. 
 “People feel more secure about their card," said SNAP recipient Susan Carpenter.
 As for Cooper, she supports the new security features.
 “I think it's a good thing; it'd be more security for us to protect ourselves from hackers and scammers,” she said. "Everybody needs that."
 Despite the recent decline, reported Lynchburg SNAP theft in October was about ten times higher than the average monthly amount reported during the first half of 2026. 
 Between January and July, the average reported stolen total in Lynchburg was roughly $2,000, according to Lynchburg Human Services.
 Now, the prior SNAP cards are set to expire this month, 60 days after the new ones were mailed out.
 Morgan said she hopes fraud levels will continue to decrease in the Hill City as the old cards phase out. 
 Morgan also urged recipients to activate their new cards, saying it is an easy step to prevent fraud. 
 Anyone who has not received one in the mail can visit the Lynchburg Human Services office at 99 9th St, Lynchburg, for assistance.
